title: To award a Congressional Gold Medal to the 65th Infantry Regiment, known as the Borinqueneers.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on May 19, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Directs the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the Senate to make appropriate arrangements for the award, on behalf of Congress, of a single gold medal in honor of the 65th Infantry Regiment, known as the Borinqueneers, in recognition of its pioneering military service, devotion to duty, and many acts of valor in the face of adversity.

Requires the medal to be given to the Smithsonian Institution for display. Expresses the sense of Congress that the Smithsonian shall make the medal available for display elsewhere, particularly at appropriate locations associated with the 65th Infantry Regiment, including locations in Puerto Rico.

summary.headline: Congress directed that a gold medal honoring the 65th Infantry Regiment, known as the Borinqueneers, be awarded and given to the Smithsonian for display.
summary.what_it_does: The law asks the House Speaker and the Senate's President pro tempore to arrange a single Congressional Gold Medal for the 65th Infantry Regiment, recognizing its military service, devotion to duty, and acts of valor. The medal is to be given to the Smithsonian Institution for display. Congress also expresses its sense that the Smithsonian should display the medal in other places tied to the regiment, including sites in Puerto Rico.
summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on June 10, 2014.
